SourceTerm: 達磨不來東土，二祖不往西天
CreatedBy: Codex Iriya construction cohort 001 lane C clean packet

Senses.PreferredTarget: Bodhidharma does not come east and the Second Patriarch does not go west
AlternateTargets: Bodhidharma never comes to the eastern land, and Huike never goes to the western heaven
Bodhidharma does not travel east while Huike does not travel west
Senses.Note: Four deployments across four works preserve the complete balanced formula as a case, challenge, and hall verdict.

Occurrences.Kwic: 知有者，達磨不來東土，二祖不往西天。不知有者，誰知當面蹉過，迢迢十萬八千。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X82/X82n1571.xml). Complete Five Lamps (Vols. 34–120). Zhuyuan Shigui says that for one who knows, Bodhidharma does not come east and the Second Patriarch does not go west.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: Zhuyuan Shigui: the heading names 溫州龍翔竹庵士珪禪師 and 上堂 assigns him the exact formula.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂。「雪峰謂玄沙曰：『備頭陀何不遍參去？』沙曰：『達磨不來東土，二祖不往西天。』」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB369.xml). Recorded Sayings at Tianhua Monastery. Xuansha Shibei utters the quoted headword-bearing answer; Zhe’an Jingfan raises the Xuefeng–Xuansha case and comments on it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂，僧問：古人道：達磨不來東土，二祖不往西天。還端的也無？師云：目前無闍黎，座上無老僧。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1412.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Gulin Qingmao. an unnamed monk asks whether the old saying that Bodhidharma does not come east and the Second Patriarch does not go west is exact.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: an unnamed monk: 僧問 owns the exact headword-bearing question and 師云 begins Gulin Qingmao’s response.

Occurrences.Kwic: 因雪峰召曰：備頭陀何不徧參去？師曰：達磨不來東土，二祖不往西天。峰然之。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X66/X66n1297.xml). Dharma Grove of the Tradition’s Mirror. Xuansha Shibei answers Xuefeng that Bodhidharma does not come east and the Second Patriarch does not go west.

Senses.Explanation: “Bodhidharma does not come east and the Second Patriarch does not go west” cancels the geographic journey on both sides of the transmission story. Named speakers wield the balanced counterfactual to test whether arrival, departure, and inherited teaching are being located in travel. Zhuyuan Shigui contrasts those who know with those who miss the formula face to face. Zhe’an Jingfan raises the Xuansha exchange as a public case. An unnamed monk puts the old saying to Gulin Qingmao, who answers without explaining it geographically. Xuansha Shibei gives the formula when Xuefeng asks why he does not travel widely to visit teachers.
